title: Medication Safety — WHO Framework
content: WHO identifies medication-related harm as a major patient-safety concern and highlights high-risk situations, polypharmacy, and transitions of care as important areas for action. Medication safety requires attention across the entire medication-use process and across care settings. The WHO Medication Without Harm initiative aims to reduce severe and avoidable medication-related harm globally.

title: The Medication-Use Process
content: Medication safety can be affected during prescribing, transcribing, dispensing, administration, and monitoring. Safety therefore depends on both medication-specific factors and healthcare-system processes. Understanding the full medication-use process helps identify where errors are most likely to occur and what safeguards are most important at each stage.

title: Medication Reconciliation
content: Medication reconciliation is the process of maintaining and communicating accurate medication information when medication regimens change or when patients move between care settings. The Joint Commission emphasizes maintaining accurate medication information and communicating it appropriately. Reconciliation should compare current medication orders with all medications the patient has been taking to identify and resolve discrepancies.

title: High-Risk Medication Situations
content: High-risk medication situations may involve high-alert medicines, patient and provider factors, and system factors. The pharmacy domain should focus on safe medication-management processes rather than independently diagnosing or treating patients. High-alert medications bear a heightened risk of causing significant patient harm when used in error, and require additional safeguards in prescribing, dispensing, and administration.

title: Medications During Transitions of Care
content: Medication information should be reviewed carefully during transitions because discrepancies can contribute to medication-related harm. Transitions between care settings are particularly high-risk moments for medication errors. A structured approach to medication review at transitions, including reconciliation of the medication list, communication with the patient and receiving providers, and clear documentation, supports medication safety.

title: Pharmacy Agent Scope and Boundaries
content: The Pharmacy Agent does not prescribe or independently recommend medication for a specific patient. It does not invent doses, contraindications, interactions, or formulary status. It uses current authoritative medication references where medication-specific facts are required and answers only from retrieved pharmacy knowledge. Medication information must be verified against current authoritative sources before clinical application.

title: Pharmacy Knowledge Sources
content: This knowledge base draws on: (1) World Health Organization, Medication without harm: Policy brief (2024). (2) WHO, Medication safety in high-risk situations (2019). (3) Joint Commission, National Performance Goal 14: Effectively Managing Medications. (4) Joint Commission, Maintaining and Communicating Patient Medication Information — Medication Reconciliation (updated 2026).
